requirements_clarity.label: M
requirements_clarity.gaps: The task required differentiating three plugins needing a brand-new onSessionStart + buildXHookConfig helper (claude, gemini, kimi — confirmed by new buildClaudeHookConfig/buildGeminiHookConfig/buildKimiHookConfig functions and new import of HookProcessingConfig) from three needing only one added call inside an already-existing onSessionStart (codemie-code, opencode, copilot-cli — confirmed by their pre-existing buildHookConfig/buildCopilotHookConfig helpers). Each of claude/gemini/kimi's new handlers also carries an explicit code comment establishing the non-obvious rule that the new call must NOT duplicate processEvent(SessionStart), since native hooks.json already routes SessionStart through codemie-hook -> handleSessionStart. This split and the new lifecycle-test naming/placement convention (*.plugin.lifecycle.test.ts, new for 5 of 6 sites) had to be worked out during implementation rather than being fully specified upfront.

technical_risk.label: S
technical_risk.risk_factors: All six call sites reuse the already-existing, already-tested reconcileStaleSessions function with the established non-blocking fire-and-forget .catch(...) + logger.debug pattern — no new runtime logic, no new control flow beyond wiring. The one real risk (duplicating native-hook-driven SessionStart processing for claude/gemini/kimi) is explicitly called out in code comments at each of those three sites and is directly asserted against in tests ('does not duplicate processEvent(SessionStart)').
technical_risk.mitigation: Non-blocking .catch with debug-level logging at every site so a reconciliation failure never affects a live session launch; new/extended lifecycle test files per plugin assert reconciliation fires exactly once, is called with the correct agent name and env, and never throws; code review approved with 0 blocking findings; QA gates HITL-approved with 16 pre-existing unrelated failures confirmed via worktree checks (none attributable to this change).
